title: Math · Grade 2
description: An original starter path: build the idea, work an example, then try it. A focused introduction, ready to grow with your class.
framework: Original introductory mathematics practice; suggested grade placement, not a complete standards syllabus.
sequenceNote: Suggested teaching sequence, not mandated unit order.
alignmentNote: Starter course; not full grade-level coverage.

lessons.title: Hundreds, tens, ones
lessons.reading: Each place is ten times the value of the place to its right. Read a three-digit number by grouping its hundreds, tens and ones.
lessons.easyReading: Each place is ten times the value of the place to its right. Read a three-digit number by grouping its hundreds, tens and ones.
lessons.expertReading: Each place is ten times the value of the place to its right. Read a three-digit number by grouping its hundreds, tens and ones. A zero can hold an empty place so the other digits retain their intended values.
lessons.worked: 407 contains four hundreds, zero tens and seven ones.
steps: 407 contains four hundreds, zero tens and seven ones.

application.prompt: What is the value of 6 in 362?
application.explanation: 60. Each place is ten times the value of the place to its right. Read a three-digit number by grouping its hundreds, tens and ones.

vocab.definition: The value a digit has because of its position.

lessons.practice: Explain how place value helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 60. Each place is ten times the value of the place to its right. Read a three-digit number by grouping its hundreds, tens and ones.

lessons.title: Regroup an addition
lessons.reading: When ones total ten or more, exchange ten ones for one ten. The quantity stays the same; only its grouping changes.
lessons.easyReading: When ones total ten or more, exchange ten ones for one ten. The quantity stays the same; only its grouping changes.
lessons.expertReading: When ones total ten or more, exchange ten ones for one ten. The quantity stays the same; only its grouping changes. Regrouping preserves value because ten ones and one ten represent equal amounts.
lessons.worked: For 28 + 16, 8 + 6 = 14 ones. Regroup as one ten and four ones; the total is 44.
steps: Regroup as one ten and four ones; the total is 44.

application.explanation: 62. When ones total ten or more, exchange ten ones for one ten. The quantity stays the same; only its grouping changes.

vocab.definition: Exchange equal quantities between place-value units.

lessons.practice: Explain how regroup helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 62. When ones total ten or more, exchange ten ones for one ten. The quantity stays the same; only its grouping changes.

lessons.title: Subtract with an exchange
lessons.reading: Exchange one ten for ten ones when there are not enough ones to subtract. Keep track of the reduced tens.
lessons.easyReading: Exchange one ten for ten ones when there are not enough ones to subtract. Keep track of the reduced tens.
lessons.expertReading: Exchange one ten for ten ones when there are not enough ones to subtract. Keep track of the reduced tens. An exchange changes a number’s representation without changing its value.
lessons.worked: For 52 − 28, write 52 as four tens and twelve ones. Subtract to get two tens and four ones.
steps: For 52 − 28, write 52 as four tens and twelve ones
Subtract to get two tens and four ones.

application.explanation: 26. Exchange one ten for ten ones when there are not enough ones to subtract. Keep track of the reduced tens.

vocab.definition: Find what remains or the difference between quantities.

lessons.practice: Explain how subtract helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 26. Exchange one ten for ten ones when there are not enough ones to subtract. Keep track of the reduced tens.

lessons.title: Read an array
lessons.reading: An array arranges objects in equal rows and columns. Add the equal rows to find the total.
lessons.easyReading: An array arranges objects in equal rows and columns. Add the equal rows to find the total.
lessons.expertReading: An array arranges objects in equal rows and columns. Add the equal rows to find the total. Turning an array shows why reversing the factors preserves a product.
lessons.worked: Three rows of four dots contain 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 dots.
steps: Three rows of four dots contain 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 dots.

application.prompt: How many dots are in four rows of three?
application.explanation: 12. An array arranges objects in equal rows and columns. Add the equal rows to find the total.

vocab.definition: An arrangement of objects in equal rows and columns.

lessons.practice: Explain how array helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 12. An array arranges objects in equal rows and columns. Add the equal rows to find the total.

lessons.title: Partition a whole
lessons.reading: Equal shares must have the same size. The number of shares tells whether we call them halves, thirds or fourths.
lessons.easyReading: Equal shares must have the same size. The number of shares tells whether we call them halves, thirds or fourths.
lessons.expertReading: Equal shares must have the same size. The number of shares tells whether we call them halves, thirds or fourths. Equal area does not require every share to have the same shape.
lessons.worked: A rectangle split into four equal areas has four fourths. Each part is one fourth.
steps: A rectangle split into four equal areas has four fourths

application.prompt: A whole is split into three equal shares. What is each share?
application.explanation: One third. Equal shares must have the same size. The number of shares tells whether we call them halves, thirds or fourths.

vocab.definition: Parts of a whole that have the same size.

lessons.practice: Explain how equal shares helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: One third. Equal shares must have the same size. The number of shares tells whether we call them halves, thirds or fourths.
